fields.meta_description: What an ACH form asks for, who fills it in, and an online version that emails each payer a signed copy and logs every debit.
fields.h1: Build an ACH Form That Records Every Authorization
fields.hero_description: An ACH form lets a business debit or credit a bank account. Describe who pays and when, and Emergent builds the form and keeps a record of every signature.
fields.features_heading: What an ACH Form Has to Say
fields.features_subheading: A blank PDF collects two numbers and a signature. These six features cover the rest of the authorization.
fields.feature_1:
Terms printed above the signature

Places the amount and the debit date right above the signature line, with the way to cancel next to them. Nacha expects a consumer debit authorization to state its terms clearly.
fields.feature_2:
A copy in the payer's inbox

Emails each payer the terms they signed the moment they submit, with a cancel link at the top. Nobody on your team has to dig up the signed record and send it by hand later.
fields.feature_3:
Debits run by the processor you connect

Passes each signed authorization to Stripe or any processor with an API, which runs the debits on schedule. Every debit in your table points back to the authorization behind it.
fields.feature_4:
Credit forms for paying vendors

Builds the other direction too: a vendor enrollment form that asks for a taxpayer ID with the bank details. Approved bills then go into a bank file that carries those details.
fields.feature_5:
Two years of records, kept for you

Keeps each signed authorization, plus any later cancellation, together in a database you own. Nacha has originators keep each one for two years after it ends or is revoked.
fields.feature_6:
Code your engineers can take over

Exports the full codebase to GitHub on paid plans. An engineer can add NACHA file exports for your bank's portal later, or you can describe that change and let Emergent write it.

fields.usecase_heading: ACH Forms for Every Kind of Payer
fields.tab_content_1:
Rent debited on the 1st, signed once

Tenants at Maple Court sign once for rent of $1,850, debited on the 1st of each month. The amount and the date appear above the signature, with the cancellation route beside them. A signed copy reaches the tenant's inbox as soon as they submit, and Stripe runs each debit against that authorization.
fields.tab_content_2:
Three invoices paid, one remittance email

Accounts payable at Northwind Foods sends suppliers one enrollment link. Each supplier adds bank details and a remittance inbox. On payment day, approved bills go into one bank file. Harbor Supply gets a single deposit of $4,210 for three invoices, with an email listing each one.
fields.tab_content_3:
Tuition of $9,600 in eight equal debits

Families at Ridgeview Academy can pay tuition in eight monthly debits of $1,200 instead of one large check. Parents choose the plan on a phone and see the full schedule before they sign. The bursar's dashboard tracks each family's next debit and shows six left once two have run.
fields.tab_content_4:
One click to cancel, and the next debit is gone

Members of Northside Fitness cancel from the same link that delivered their signed copy. When Dana Ortiz cancels her $59 monthly dues, the next debit comes off the schedule before Stripe can run it. Sam Lee, the billing lead, gets a Slack direct message, and the cancellation is saved beside her original terms.

fields.howto_title: How to Make an ACH Form
fields.howto_description: Write the terms before the fields. The order below follows what a payer reads, then what your team has to keep.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide whether you debit or credit
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write the terms in plain words
fields.howto_step_1_des: Debit or credit decides the wording. A debit form lets you pull money from the payer's account for rent or dues. A credit form, such as a vendor enrollment, lets you send money in. Most businesses keep the two as separate forms.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Collect the account holder's name, the bank, the routing number, the account number and whether the account is checking or savings. On vendor forms, add the company name and taxpayer ID, because accounts payable matches each payment against both.
fields.howto_step_3_des: State the amount or how it is calculated, the first debit date and how often it repeats. Title the page plainly as an authorization, because Nacha wants it readily identifiable as one.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Spell out how the payer revokes the authorization and how much notice you need before the next debit. Nacha requires consumer debit authorizations to explain revocation. A cancel link inside the signed copy is the route payers find first.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell Emergent who pays on what schedule. Name the processor that runs the debits too. From that description, Emergent builds the form with a signature step and stores each authorization in a database you own.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Nacha requires originators to give consumers a copy of their debit authorization. Send it the moment they sign. Put the amount and the cancel link at the top of the email, where a payer checking a debit looks first.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Keep the version each payer signed
fields.howto_step_7_des: Save each payer's wording with the date they signed it. Terms change over time, and a disputed debit has to match the version in force on the day it ran. Edit the terms for new payers only, and leave existing records untouched.

plan.angle: The top 10 is blank paper: the IRS Form 3881 PDF, sample forms from a bank, a town finance office, a college and a contractor, a QuickBooks community thread and a Ramp explainer. Each one collects routing and account numbers and stops there. This page answers the searcher's questions first (what the form is, who fills it in, where a bank's version lives), lists what Nacha expects a debit authorization to say, then shows the online version: the customer signs the exact terms, gets a copy, can cancel from a link, and every debit points back to the authorization that allowed it.

claims_to_source: An ACH authorization form gives a business permission to debit or credit a bank account and collects the account holder's name, bank, routing number, account number, account type and a signature
Nacha rules require a consumer debit authorization to be in writing and signed or similarly authenticated, readily identifiable, with clear terms, and to explain how the customer can revoke it
The originator must give the consumer a copy of a debit authorization
Originators keep a record of each authorization for two years after it is terminated or revoked
IRS Form 3881 is the ACH vendor and miscellaneous payment enrollment form federal agencies use to pay vendors by ACH
An ACH file is a NACHA-format text file of 94-character records: a file header, batch headers, entry details, batch controls and a file control
Zelle payments between enrolled users typically arrive within minutes
Stripe accepts ACH Direct Debit from US bank accounts, including recurring debits under a mandate the customer accepts
